entities.summary:
Jaime or James of Portugal, also known as James of Coimbra, James of Lusitania, was a Portuguese infante (prince) of the House of Aviz, and a bishop and cardinal of the Roman Catholic Church. He played a crucial role in the Portuguese Reconquista, leading the Christian forces to victory over the Moorish kingdom of Al-Andalus in the 13th century. This achievement had significant implications for the balance of power in the Iberian Peninsula and set the stage for Portugal's emergence as a major European power.

Born in the early 14th century, James rose to prominence during the reign of King Dinis of Portugal. He was appointed as the Bishop of Coimbra and later became a cardinal, earning the respect and admiration of his contemporaries. James's leadership and strategic prowess were instrumental in the Christian reconquest of the Iberian Peninsula, which was completed in 1249. This triumph marked the end of Moorish rule in Portugal and established James as a key figure in shaping the country's future.

James's legacy extends beyond his military victories, as he also played a significant role in promoting the arts and education during his time. He was a patron of the arts and architecture, and his court attracted scholars and artists from across Europe. James's influence can still be seen in the beautiful architecture and cultural heritage of Portugal today.

James of Coimbra died on September 5, 1459, leaving behind a lasting impact on Portuguese history and culture. His bravery, strategic thinking, and commitment to the arts and education have made him a celebrated figure in Portuguese history.
